title: Great God! and Wilt Thou Condescend
description: Great God! and Wilt Thou Condescend in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 448, “A Child's Prayer”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Great God! and wilt Thou con-de-scend To be my Fa-ther and my Friend? I but a child, and Thou so high, The Lord of earth and air and sky!

lines: Great God! and wilt Thou condescend
To be my Father and my Friend?
I but a child, — and Thou so high,
The Lord of earth and air and sky!
Art Thou my Father? — Let me be
A meek, obedient child to Thee;
And try, in word and deed and thought,
To serve and please Thee as I ought.
Art Thou my Father? — I'll depend
Upon the care of such a friend;
And only wish to do and be
Art Thou my Father? — Then, at last,
When all my days on earth are past,
Send down, and take me, in Thy love,
To be Thy better child above.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
